requirements.heading: Introduction
requirements.text: MTAs generating the header fields SHOULD usually include a mailto based command, in addition to any other protocols used, in order to support users who do not have access to non-mail-based protocols.

requirements.heading: Introduction
requirements.text: Many list managers, especially as the proposal first gains acceptance, MAY choose to implement only one or two of the fields.

requirements.heading: The Command Syntax
requirements.text: MTAs MUST NOT insert whitespace within the brackets, but client applications should treat any whitespace, that might be inserted by poorly behaved MTAs, as characters to ignore.

requirements.heading: The Command Syntax
requirements.text: A list of multiple, alternate, URLs MAY be specified by a comma- separated list of angle-bracket enclosed URLs.

requirements.heading: The Command Syntax
requirements.text: However, systems using such syntaxes SHOULD still take advantage of the List-Help field to provide the user with detailed instructions as needed or - perhaps more usefully - provide access to some form of structured command interface such as an HTML-based form.

requirements.heading: The Command Syntax
requirements.text: To allow for future extension, client applications MUST follow the following guidelines for handling the contents of the header fields described in this document:

requirements.heading: The Command Syntax
requirements.text: 1) Except where noted for specific fields, if the content of the field (following any leading whitespace, including comments) begins with any character other than the opening angle bracket '<', the field SHOULD be ignored.

requirements.heading: The Command Syntax
requirements.text: 2) Any characters following an angle bracket enclosed URL SHOULD be ignored, unless a comma is the first non-whitespace/comment character after the closing angle bracket.

requirements.heading: The Command Syntax
requirements.text: 3) If a sub-item (comma-separated item) within the field is not an angle-bracket enclosed URL, the remainder of the field (the current, and all subsequent, sub-items) SHOULD be ignored.

requirements.heading: The List Header Fields
requirements.text: The fields implemented on a given list SHOULD be included on all messages distributed by the list (including command responses to individual users), and on other messages where the message clearly applies to one distinct list.

requirements.heading: The List Header Fields
requirements.text: There MUST be no more than one of each field present in any given message.

requirements.heading: The List Header Fields
requirements.text: These fields MUST only be generated by mailing lists, not end users.

requirements.heading: List-Help
requirements.text: It would be acceptable for a list manager to include only this field, since by definition it SHOULD direct the user to complete instructions for all other commands.

requirements.heading: List-Post
requirements.text: This is typically the address of the list, but MAY be a moderator, or potentially some other form of submission.

requirements.heading: List-Owner
requirements.text: The URL MAY contain the address of a administrator for the list, the mail system administrator, or any other person who can handle user contact for the list.

requirements.heading: Supporting Nested Lists
requirements.text: Sublists SHOULD remove the parent list's List-Help, List-Subscribe, List-Unsubscribe and List-Owner fields, and SHOULD insert their own versions of those fields.

requirements.heading: Supporting Nested Lists
requirements.text: If the sublist provides its own archive, it SHOULD replace the List- Archive with its own.

requirements.heading: Supporting Nested Lists
requirements.text: Otherwise, it MUST leave the List-Archive field untouched.

requirements.heading: Supporting Nested Lists
requirements.text: Dependant on how postings to the list are handled, the sublist MAY replace the List-Post field.

requirements.heading: Acknowledgements
requirements.text: If using a dialog interface (or other feedback element) the client application MUST include an option for the user to review (and possibly modify) the message before it is sent.
